posts.title: The Land That Sat Empty
posts.topic: Kelo v. City of New London (2005): city took homes for private development; Pfizer left in 2009, land stayed vacant

slides.text:
In 2005, the Supreme Court ruled New London, Connecticut could **take homes for a private development**.

The homes came down. Then **Pfizer, the big neighbor the plan was built around, left town** in 2009, and the land sat empty for years.

posts.caption:
A city won at the Supreme Court, then the project it fought for was never built. Was the ruling right?

#JuryJuice #EminentDomain #SupremeCourt

Source: Kelo v. City of New London (2005)

A judge ordered it sold. The city bought it and **had it destroyed**.
The Supreme Court later ruled 7 to 2: **never a boat**.
